I live off grid on several acres.  I'm clearing land for pasture.  This happened last week.

I've been using a chainsaw to drop & cut trees all morning & I'm ready to stop for lunch.  before I do that, I need to knock down a couple stumps I left long because of the angle I had to cut them down.

The last stump isn't more than 7" across but has sort of a twist in it because of the way the tree grew.  I already made a horizontal cut earlier before deciding to come back later to finish it off.

I start cutting another horizontal line opposite my cut from earlier with the intent of connecting the two and getting the stump to fall.  This second cut doesn't meet up with the first like I want so I start cutting in from the first cut again thinking there's probably just a small bit left in the middle.

Having cut all the way through the middle, I take my hand off the throttle and swipe at the stump to knock it down.  The stump doesn't move.  Not expecting the resistance,  my hand bounces back, causing my balance to shift. Instinctively my other hand, still holding the saw, jerks up, bringing the saw up just enough to catch the wrist of the hand that swiped at the trunk.  The chain hadn't come to a complete stop and the blood was immediate.

Dropping the saw, I begin running back towards the house (140 paces), grabbing my wrist with my other hand and holding it over my head. All the while cursing myself for doing something so ignorant.  Im on a private dirt road with 2 other neighbors, neither of which are home right now.  Literally nobody can hear me scream and visions of me bleeding out and dieing in my driveway begin taking shape.

The thought of calling an ambulance enters my mind...but it'd be too late by the time they get here...I'd be better off driving myself...but I need to stop the blood first...at least well enough to drive myself.  this lifestyle doesn't come with good health insurance and the cost of an ambulance ride would suck if it doesn't turn out to be life-threatening.

Reaching the house, I run onto the porch and grab a white t-shirt draped on a chair as I head for the kitchen sink. 

I wrap and tie the shirt on my wrist as tight and quick as I can. There's too much blood and I can't yet tell where exactly, my wrist is bleeding from.

I watch the shirt for a few moments to make sure blood isn't seeping out from under it.  It's not.  I think I stopped the bleeding. 

I'm still not sure how bad it is.  I feel no pain...probably from adrenaline.  Im not sure how much blood I've lost. I drink a couple cups of water, grab my car keys and head back outside.

I can hear the chainsaw still runnng in the distance. I open the door and reach in to start my car.  I'm still not seeing any significant blood seeping into the shirt.  Maybe it's not life threatening.  I toss the keys onto the seat and go to shut the chainsaw off.

Walking back toward the saw, I come across my hat and ear protection. I don't remember taking them off.   No sign of the goggles.

The saw is idling on it side.  After it's shut off I notice blood on the still standing stump.  Fucking stump.

Walking back onto the porch, I can see blood smeared on the door and along the floor. My hand is turning purple and  I need to know exactly how bad I've hurt myself.  I need the first aid kit in the bathroom.

Back in the kitchen,  I open the kit and dig out all the gauze, wrapping, medical tape and the biggest band-aids I can find.  I need to see the damage before I know what im going to do.

Over the sink, I begin to untie the shirt.  There's two gashes below my pinky finger where my hand meets my wrist.  They stretch diagonally down into the side of my wrist and end about an inch from the center.  It's still bleeding but it's not life-threatening.   I can fix this but not with band-aids.

I run some water over it and it stings.  Im still not feeling any pain.  Adrenaline is a hell of a drug.  I start tearing off medical tape and sticking pieces  on the chair next to me.

I need two gauze pads just to cover both gashes.  Its not easy to cover and wrap the entire wound with one hand but I get it done and use the pieces of tape to help keep it together. It's not pretty but it'll work for now.

The entire ordeal has taken about 10 minutes away from my lunch time. I cook up and quickly eat a grilled cheese sandwich before going back outside. I still have a few hours before dark and this pasture isn't going to clear itself.
